survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD country note does not analyze student microdata from an ILSA (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIRLS) and therefore does not define a sampling frame, student-level analytic dataset, or any associated complex survey weights. The document describes governance structures and expenditure shares across federal, state (estados), and municipal (municipios) levels for Mexico’s adult skills system. As a result, there is no plausible weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) to apply, and no replicate-weight scheme (e.g., BRR/jackknife) is relevant. If analysts were to extend this note with ILSA microdata, they would need to use the official ILSA sampling weights and PV procedures for the specific assessment and cycle; this note itself provides none.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a governance and policy mapping country note rather than an empirical analysis of student achievement or other PV-based outcomes. Because it does not use ILSA microdata with cognitive achievement scales, plausible values (PV) are not generated or analyzed, and missing-data handling for PVs is not part of the study design. The note focuses on institutional responsibilities (strategy, intelligence, implementation, funding, delivery) across government levels, so PV and missing-data procedures are not applicable to the reported content.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No ILSA or other student-level dataset is analyzed. The note uses descriptive information to characterize Mexico’s adult skills system governance across federal, state, and municipal levels; therefore, there is no analytic subsample selection, task/module restriction, or missing-case exclusion.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD country note provides a descriptive overview of how Mexico’s adult skills system is governed across federal, state (estados), and municipal (municipios) levels. It reports that the system is relatively decentralised: national ministries define overarching strategies and frameworks, while subnational authorities retain flexibility to adapt and implement programmes. The note structures responsibilities by policy area—VET/HVET, ALMP/CET, and Adult Education (AE)—and by governance functions (strategy, intelligence, implementation, funding, delivery), using tables to show which level performs which function. It also quantifies the subnational share of general government expenditure at 43.0% and describes key stakeholder roles (ministries, national agencies, state institutes, municipal employment agencies, and social partners). No student assessment data, sampling design, scaling, or performance metrics are analyzed, so there are no ML or PV-based results.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is not an empirical large-scale assessment study and does not conduct ML prediction/classification on ILSA microdata. Consequently, fields such as total_students, PV handling, missing-data handling, and main_findings (structured predictive outcomes) are not populated because the document is a policy/governance description rather than an analysis of student outcomes.
